# Load packages

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| code-summary: "Load packages"
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# remotes::install_github("16EAGLE/moveVis")

library(tidyverse)
packages <- c("amt", "lubridate", 
              "SDLfilter",
              "terra", 
              "beepr", "tictoc",
              "moveVis", "move2", "sf")
walk(packages, require, character.only = T)

```

# Import GPS tracking data

```{r}
#| label: import_data
#| code-summary: "Import GPS tracking data"

pig_gps <- read_csv("data/pig_all_steps_covs_subset_20260813.csv")

pig_gps <- pig_gps %>% 
  mutate(
    t1_  = with_tz(t1_, tzone = "Australia/Darwin"),
    t2_ = with_tz(t2_, tzone = "Australia/Darwin")
  )
    
head(pig_gps)

# keep the relevant data for the simulations
pig_gps_betty <- pig_gps[2:2001, ]
head(pig_gps_betty)

pig_gps_betty_clean <- pig_gps_betty %>% 
  transmute(
    name = name,
    x = x1_,
    y = y1_,
    t = t1_
  )

```

# Read simulated trajectories

## All starting from the same location

```{r}

pig_sim <- read_csv("outputs/alphaearth/2026-08-17_4/deepSSF_trajectories/deepSSF_pigs_10traj_1000steps_2026-08-21.csv")
head(pig_sim)

```

## Add a timestamp to the simulated data

```{r}

start_time <- pig_gps_betty[[1, "t1_"]]
time_sequence <- rep(seq(start_time, by = "hour", length.out = 1000), 10)

pig_sim$t1_ <- time_sequence

pig_sim_clean <- pig_sim %>% 
  transmute(
    name = trajectory_id,
    x = x,
    y = y,
    t = t1_
  )

```


### Combine datasets

```{r}

combined_data <- rbind(pig_gps_betty_clean, pig_sim_clean)

```

# moveVis animation

## Convert to a `move2` object

The coordinates are in GDA94 / Geoscience Australia Lambert (EPSG:3112), so we
build an `sf` object with that CRS and transform to geographic coordinates
(EPSG:4326), which is what `moveVis` expects for the basemap services.

```{r}
#| label: make_move2
#| message: false

# label the simulated trajectories so they are distinct from the observed track,
# and so the track ids sort sensibly (sim_01 ... sim_10 rather than 1, 10, 2 ...)
move_df <- combined_data %>%
  mutate(
    name = if_else(
      name == "Betty",
      "Betty",
      sprintf("sim_%02d", suppressWarnings(as.integer(name)) + 1)
      )
  ) %>%
  arrange(name, t) %>%
  filter(!is.na(x), !is.na(y), !is.na(t))

# how much of the sequence to animate - the full sequence is ~1000 hours (~42
# days), which makes for a very long animation, so we subset by default
n_days <- 10
t_start <- min(move_df$t)
move_df <- move_df %>% filter(t <= t_start + days(n_days))

# Two quirks of moveVis 1.0.1 to work around here:
#
# 1. align_move() refers to the time column as `timestamp` internally, so the
#    time column has to be named `timestamp` (naming it `t` throws
#    "argument 1 is not a vector" inside align_move).
#
# 2. frames_spatial() reads the CRS by calling capture.output() on the printed
#    move2 object and parsing line 5. If the object is tibble-backed, that print
#    goes through print.tbl_df, and if anything in the session has replaced that
#    method the print fails with "generic function not specified". Dropping to a
#    plain data.frame sends the print through print.data.frame instead, and the
#    CRS line moveVis wants is unchanged.
move_data <- move_df %>%
  rename(timestamp = t) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%                            # not a tibble - see note 2
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 3112) %>% # GDA94 / GA Lambert
  st_transform(4326) %>%                         # WGS84 lon/lat for moveVis
  mt_as_move2(time_column = "timestamp", track_id_column = "name")

# head() rather than printing the whole object - it is a plain data.frame now,
# so it does not self-truncate the way a tibble does
head(move_data)
mt_track_id_column(move_data)
mt_time_column(move_data)

# temporal resolution of each track - Betty is at 0.5 hours (30 min), the
# simulated trajectories are at 1 hour (60 min)
tapply(mt_time_lags(move_data, units = "min"), mt_track_id(move_data),
       median, na.rm = TRUE)

```

## Align to a uniform time scale

`align_move` interpolates all tracks onto a single, regular time scale, which
resolves the mismatch between Betty's 0.5-hour fixes and the 1-hour simulated
steps. Using a resolution finer than the native fix rate (e.g. 15 minutes)
gives a smoother animation, at the cost of more frames.

```{r}
#| label: align_move
#| message: false

m <- align_move(move_data, res = units::set_units(15, "min"))

# number of frames that will be produced
length(unique(mt_time(m)))

```

## Create spatial frames

```{r}
#| label: frames_spatial
#| message: false

# observed track in red, simulated trajectories in a viridis ramp
track_ids <- levels(as.factor(mt_track_id(m)))
path_cols <- setNames(
  viridisLite::viridis(length(track_ids), end = 0.9),
  track_ids
  )
path_cols["Betty"] <- "red"

frames <- frames_spatial(
  m,
  path_colours = unname(path_cols[track_ids]),
  path_legend_title = "Track",
  # satellite imagery is much more informative than the OSM basemaps in this
  # part of Kakadu, where the OSM tiles are essentially blank
  map_service = "esri",
  map_type = "world_imagery",
  # map_service = "osm", map_type = "topographic", # alternative basemap
  alpha = 0.8,
  path_fade = TRUE,
  path_alpha = 0.75,
  tail_length = 12, # ~3 hours of tail at 15 minute resolution
  trace_show = TRUE,
  trace_size = 0.5
  ) %>%
  add_labels(x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude") %>%
  add_northarrow() %>%
  add_scalebar() %>%
  add_timestamps(type = "label") %>%
  add_progress()

length(frames)

```



```{r}
#| label: preview_frame

frames[[100]] # preview one of the frames, e.g. the 100th frame

```

## Animate the frames

With `n_days = 7` at a 15-minute resolution this is ~670 frames, which takes a
few minutes to render. Reduce `n_days`, or coarsen the `align_move` resolution
to 30 or 60 minutes, for a quicker animation.

```{r}
#| label: animate_frames
#| message: false

dir.create("outputs/moveVis", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

animate_frames(
  frames,
  out_file = paste0("outputs/moveVis/deepSSF_pigs_", Sys.Date(), ".gif"),
  fps = 50,
  width = 1600,
  height = 1600,
  res = 200,
  overwrite = TRUE
  )

```

# From aerial survey data

```{r}

n_tracks <- 300

pig_aerial_sim <- read_csv("outputs/alphaearth/2026-08-17_4/deepSSF_trajectories/deepSSF_pigs_599traj_1000steps_2026-08-21.csv")
head(pig_aerial_sim)

pig_aerial_sim <- pig_aerial_sim %>% filter(trajectory_id %in% 1:n_tracks)

```



```{r}

time_sequence <- rep(seq(start_time, by = "hour", length.out = 1000), n_tracks)
pig_aerial_sim$t <- time_sequence

move_df2 <- pig_aerial_sim %>%
  mutate(
    name = sprintf("sim_%02d", suppressWarnings(as.integer(trajectory_id)) + 1)
  ) %>%
  arrange(name, t) %>%
  filter(!is.na(x), !is.na(y), !is.na(t))

# how much of the sequence to animate - the full sequence is ~1000 hours (~42
# days), which makes for a very long animation, so we subset by default
n_days <- 7
t_start <- min(move_df2$t)
move_df2 <- move_df2 %>% filter(t <= t_start + days(n_days))

move_data <- move_df2 %>%
  rename(timestamp = t) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%                            # not a tibble - see note 2
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 3112) %>% # GDA94 / GA Lambert
  st_transform(4326) %>%                         # WGS84 lon/lat for moveVis
  mt_as_move2(time_column = "timestamp", track_id_column = "name")

# head() rather than printing the whole object - it is a plain data.frame now,
# so it does not self-truncate the way a tibble does
head(move_data)
mt_track_id_column(move_data)
mt_time_column(move_data)

# temporal resolution of each track
tapply(mt_time_lags(move_data, units = "min"), mt_track_id(move_data),
       median, na.rm = TRUE)

# align the simulated locations
m <- align_move(move_data, res = units::set_units(60, "min"))

# number of frames that will be produced
length(unique(mt_time(m)))

```

## Create spatial frames

```{r}
#| label: frames_spatial
#| message: false

# observed track in red, simulated trajectories in a viridis ramp
track_ids <- levels(as.factor(mt_track_id(m)))
path_cols <- setNames(
  viridisLite::turbo(length(track_ids), end = 1.0),
  track_ids
  )

frames <- frames_spatial(
  m,
  path_colours = unname(path_cols[track_ids]),
  path_legend_title = "Track",
  map_service = "esri",
  map_type = "world_imagery",
  alpha = 0.8,
  path_fade = TRUE,
  path_alpha = 0.75,
  path_legend = FALSE,
  tail_length = 12, # ~3 hours of tail at 15 minute resolution
  trace_show = TRUE,
  trace_size = 0.5
  ) %>%
  add_labels(x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude") %>%
  add_northarrow() %>%
  add_scalebar() %>%
  add_timestamps(type = "label") %>%
  add_progress()

length(frames)
length(unique(unname(path_cols[track_ids])))

```



```{r}
#| label: preview_frame

frames[[50]] # preview one of the frames, e.g. the 100th frame

```

## Animate the frames

With `n_days = 7` at a 15-minute resolution this is ~670 frames, which takes a
few minutes to render. Reduce `n_days`, or coarsen the `align_move` resolution
to 30 or 60 minutes, for a quicker animation.

```{r}
#| label: animate_frames
#| message: false

dir.create("outputs/moveVis", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

aspect_ratio <- 1.5

# set output pixel dimensions to match
out_height <- 1600
out_width <- round(out_height * 1.5)

animate_frames(
  frames,
  out_file = paste0("outputs/moveVis/deepSSF_pigs_aerial_survey", Sys.Date(), ".gif"),
  fps = 50,
  width = out_width,
  height = out_height,
  res = 200,
  overwrite = TRUE
  )

```
